title: Fast speech and contractions
goal: Recognize the contractions of fast spoken French (chais pas, j'suis, y'a, t'sais, t'es, faut) and rebuild the full standard sentence in your head.

items.fr: je ne sais pas → j'sais pas → chais pas
items.en: how fast speech shortens words (dropped ne, dropped e, merged sounds)

drills.prompt: “Y'a pas de lait.” What's the full standard sentence?
options: Il n'y a pas de lait.
drills.explain: [[y'a]] = [[il y a]]. In speech, [[il]] shrinks to [[i]] and [[ne]] disappears: [[il n'y a pas]] → [[y'a pas]].
[[je ne sais pas]] → [[j'sais pas]] → [[chais pas]]: the [[j]] and [[s]] merge into a [[ch]] sound.
Before a vowel, [[tu]] often loses its [[u]] in speech: [[t'es]], [[t'as]], [[t'avais]]. Never write it in formal texts.

items.note: Recognize it; when you write, always [[je ne sais pas]].

items.en: there is, there are (fast speech for il y a)

items.note: Extremely frequent in Québec, often at the end of a sentence: [[C'est pas facile, t'sais.]]

items.en: you're (informal, fast speech for tu es)
you have (informal, fast speech for tu as)
gotta, you have to (fast speech for il faut)

example.fr: Il est arrivé genre à minuit.

steps.title: Lunch break, real speed
steps.intro: Native speakers don't say [[je ne sais pas]]: they say something like *chè pa*. Textbook French and spoken French are the same language, but at full speed, small words shrink or vanish. Listen first, then compare what you hear with what it means.

blocks.title: On mange où ?
blocks.context: Alex (from Lyon) and Sofia (from Montréal) are colleagues at a tech company in Montréal. It's noon, they're hungry and talking fast.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.en: (Tu as faim ? On mange où ?) Are you hungry? Where are we eating?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Chais pas. Y'a le petit resto vietnamien, mais y'a toujours du monde le midi.
lines.en: (Je ne sais pas. Il y a le petit restaurant vietnamien, mais il y a toujours beaucoup de monde le midi.) Dunno. There's the little Vietnamese place, but it's always packed at lunch.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.fr: Ouais, mais c'est pas grave. J'suis pas pressé aujourd'hui.
lines.en: (Oui, mais ce n'est pas grave. Je ne suis pas pressé aujourd'hui.) Yeah, but no big deal. I'm not in a hurry today.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Moi, oui. Faut que j'finisse mon rapport avant deux heures, t'sais.
lines.en: (Moi, oui. Il faut que je finisse mon rapport avant deux heures, tu sais.) I am. I gotta finish my report before two, you know.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.fr: T'es sérieuse ? Ben, on prend un truc à emporter, alors.
lines.en: (Tu es sérieuse ? Eh bien, on prend quelque chose à emporter, alors.) Seriously? Well, let's get something to go, then.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Parfait. Qu'est-ce tu prends ? Moi, genre, une soupe pis un rouleau.
lines.en: (Parfait. Qu'est-ce que tu prends ? Moi, par exemple, une soupe et un rouleau.) Perfect. Whatcha getting? Me, like, a soup and a roll.

blocks.title: Sofia's voice message
blocks.context: That evening, Sofia sends a voice message to her friend Mei. She speaks fast and informally.
blocks.fr: Allô, c'est moi. J'suis crevée, t'sais pas comment. Y'a eu un bug sur le serveur à trois heures, pis là, faut que j'recommence tout demain matin. Fait que, ben, chais pas si j'peux aller au cinéma avec toi. T'es libre samedi, plutôt ? Texte-moi.
blocks.en:
Hi, it's me. I'm exhausted, you have no idea. There was a bug on the server at three, and now I have to start everything over tomorrow morning. So, well, I don't know if I can go to the movies with you. Are you free on Saturday instead? Text me.

Full standard version: Je suis crevée, tu ne sais pas à quel point. Il y a eu un bogue sur le serveur à trois heures, et maintenant, il faut que je recommence tout demain matin. Donc, eh bien, je ne sais pas si je peux aller au cinéma avec toi. Es-tu libre samedi, plutôt ?

blocks.prompt: What does Sofia propose to Mei?
options: To go to the movies on Saturday instead
To go to the movies tonight
blocks.explain: [[chais pas si j'peux aller au cinéma avec toi. T'es libre samedi, plutôt ?]] = I don't know if I can go… Are you free on Saturday instead?

blocks.prompt: In “Faut que j'recommence tout”, what has disappeared?
options: il (before faut) and the e of je
blocks.explain: [[Il faut que je recommence]] → [[Faut que j'recommence]]. The subjunctive is still there!

blocks.title: What happens at full speed
head: Process
Written
Spoken
Sounds like
rows: Je ne sais pas. / Ce n'est pas grave.
Je sais pas. / C'est pas grave.
je suis, le petit, que je finisse
je sais, je suis, je pense
il y a, il faut, tu es, tu as, il est
blocks.note: Process 3 happens because [[j]] loses its voice before [[s]], [[p]], [[t]], [[k]] and becomes [[ch]]. That's why [[je sais pas]] sounds like *chè pa*.

blocks.title: Recognition table: heard → meant
head: You hear
It means
English
rows: il y a / il n'y a pas

blocks.title: Fillers that carry meaning
blocks.body:
- **[[ben]]** (from [[bien]]): hesitation or obviousness. [[Ben oui !]] = Well, of course!
- **[[ouais]]** (France) / **[[ouin]]** (Québec): yeah. [[Ouin…]] said slowly often means *hmm, not sure*.
- **[[genre]]**: like. Introduces an approximation ([[genre dix personnes]]) or an example.
- **[[t'sais]]**: you know. Asks for agreement or fills a pause.
- **[[quoi]]** at the end (France): [[C'était bizarre, quoi.]] = It was weird, you know.
- **[[là]]** (very Québécois): [[Là, j'suis fatigué.]] = Right now, I'm tired. [[Pis là…]] = and then…

**Strategy**: when you hear a burst of small sounds, don't panic. Grab the **content words** (nouns, main verbs, numbers) and rebuild the frame.

blocks.title: Recognize, don't write
blocks.body:
- **Writing contractions in formal texts**: [[J'sais pas si y'a une solution]] ✗ in an email or an exam. Write [[Je ne sais pas s'il existe une solution.]]
- **Forcing contractions when you speak**: dropping [[ne]] in casual speech is natural and fine ([[je sais pas]]). Exaggerated [[chais pas]], [[chuis]] from a learner can sound odd. Let it come naturally.
- **Thinking the negation is gone**: [[J'suis pas pressé]] is still negative! In speech, [[pas]] carries the negation alone.
- **Confusing [[y'a]] (il y a) and [[il a]]**: [[Y'a un chien]] = there's a dog. [[Il a un chien]] = he has a dog. In fast Québec speech, [[il a]] can also sound like *ya*: use the context.
- **[[t'es]] vs [[tes]]**: [[t'es]] = tu es; [[tes]] = your (plural): [[T'es avec tes amis ?]]

blocks.title: Extra contractions in Québec
blocks.body:
Québec informal speech has a few more:

- **[[a]]** for [[elle]]: [[A l'a dit]] = Elle l'a dit (She said it).
- **[[y'é]]** or **[[y'est]]** for [[il est]]: [[Y'é où ?]] = Il est où ? (Where is he?)
- **[[m'as]]** for [[je vais]]: [[M'as t'appeler]] = Je vais t'appeler (I'm gonna call you).
- **[[icitte]]** for [[ici]], **[[à soir]]** for [[ce soir]], **[[à matin]]** for [[ce matin]].
- **[[chus]]** for [[je suis]], very common: [[Chus brûlé]] = Je suis épuisé (I'm exhausted).
- **[[pus]]** for [[plus]] in a negation: [[Y'a pus de lait]] = Il n'y a plus de lait.

These are normal in casual conversation, including among educated speakers. Just like Parisians say [[chais pas]], Montrealers say [[chus]]. They are for **recognition only**: never write them in your own answers, emails or exams.

blocks.title: Why does French squeeze so much?
blocks.body: French is spoken in rhythmic groups with the stress on the last syllable. Small grammatical words ([[je]], [[le]], [[ne]], [[il]]) are unstressed, so in fast speech they shrink to a single consonant or vanish. The meaning survives because the stressed content word is still clear. That's why listening for **stressed words** (usually the last one in each group) is the key to understanding fast speech.

steps.title: Decode fast speech
steps.intro: The device voice reads these forms a little more carefully than real speakers, but the structures are authentic. For each one, rebuild the full sentence in your head.

blocks.title: Listen: written vs spoken
blocks.note: Hear the full form first, then the fast form. You don't need to produce the fast form; train your ear.

lines.en: I don't know. (fast: sounds like chè pa)

lines.fr: Il n'y a pas de problème.
Il faut que j'y aille. Faut que j'y aille.
lines.en: I have to go. (full, then fast)

blocks.fr: J'suis désolé, j'peux pas venir ce soir. Y'a un problème avec ma fille.
blocks.en: I'm sorry, I can't come tonight. There's a problem with my daughter.
blocks.prompt: What is the full standard version?
options: Je suis désolé, je ne peux pas venir ce soir. Il y a un problème avec ma fille.
Je suis désolé, je peux venir ce soir. Il a un problème avec sa fille.
J'étais désolé, je ne pouvais pas venir. Il y avait un problème.
blocks.explain: [[j'suis]] = je suis; [[j'peux pas]] = je ne peux pas; [[y'a]] = il y a.

blocks.fr: T'as vu l'heure ? Faut partir, là. Le dernier métro, y'est à minuit et demie.
blocks.en: Have you seen the time? We gotta leave now. The last metro is at half past midnight.
blocks.prompt: Why does the speaker want to leave?
blocks.explain: [[Faut partir]] = il faut partir. [[Le dernier métro, y'est à minuit et demie]] = il est à minuit et demie.

blocks.fr: Ben, chais pas, moi. Y'en a qui disent que c'est bon, mais t'sais, c'est cher en titi.
blocks.en: Well, I dunno. Some people say it's good, but you know, it's really expensive.
options: She's unsure: some say it's good, but it's very expensive
She loves it and it's cheap
She has never heard of it
blocks.explain: [[chais pas]] = I don't know; [[y'en a qui disent]] = some people say; [[en titi]] (Québec, informal) = very, a lot.

blocks.fr: Y'a pas de problème, t'inquiète pas.
accept: Y a pas de problème, t'inquiète pas.
blocks.explain: Write what you hear. In your own writing, always use the full form: [[Il n'y a pas de problème, ne t'inquiète pas.]]

steps.title: Your turn
steps.intro: Mostly decoding. A few questions bring back Québec French and interviews.

blocks.prompt: Match each spoken form with its full form.

blocks.fr: Qu'est-ce tu fais en fin de semaine ? Moi, j'suis pas mal libre.
blocks.en: What are you doing this weekend? Me, I'm pretty much free.
blocks.prompt: What is the speaker saying about herself?
blocks.explain: [[j'suis pas mal libre]] = je suis assez libre. Careful: [[pas mal]] here means *quite, pretty much*, not a negation!

blocks.prompt: Write in full standard French: “Chais pas si t'es libre.”
accept: Je ne sais pas si tu es libre.
blocks.explain: [[chais pas]] → je ne sais pas; [[t'es]] → tu es.

blocks.fr: Y'a pus de place dans le stationnement, faut que j'me stationne dans la rue.
blocks.en: There's no more room in the parking lot, I have to park on the street.
blocks.explain: [[y'a pus]] (Québec) = il n'y a plus. [[pus]] is the informal Québec pronunciation of [[plus]] in negation.

blocks.text: J'suis pas pressé. = Je ___ suis ___ pressé.
blocks.explain: In speech [[ne]] drops, but the sentence stays negative thanks to [[pas]].

blocks.prompt: “T'es avec tes parents ?” Which is the full form?
blocks.explain: [[t'es]] = tu es; [[tes]] = your (plural). Same sound, different words.

blocks.fr: Écoutez, en fait, j'pense qu'y'a un malentendu. Moi, j'ai jamais dit que c'était gratuit.
blocks.en: Listen, actually, I think there's a misunderstanding. I never said it was free.
blocks.explain: [[j'ai jamais dit]] = je n'ai jamais dit (dropped [[ne]]). [[qu'y'a]] = qu'il y a.

blocks.prompt: Write in full standard French: “Faut qu'tu viennes, y'a une surprise.”
accept: Il faut que tu viennes, il y a une surprise.
blocks.explain: [[faut qu'tu]] = il faut que tu (+ subjunctive [[viennes]]); [[y'a]] = il y a.

accept: Je sais pas, t'sais, c'est compliqué.
blocks.explain: Write what you hear ([[j'sais pas]] and [[chais pas]] sound the same). The full written form is [[Je ne sais pas, tu sais, c'est compliqué.]]

blocks.prompt: Your friend sent you this voice message (transcribed): “Salut ! Chais pas si t'as vu, mais y'a un spectacle gratuit au parc samedi. Faut arriver tôt, y'aura du monde. T'es partant ? Texte-moi, j'suis au travail jusqu'à six heures.” Rewrite it in full standard French, then reply in a correct, friendly written message.
blocks.promptFr: Réécrivez le message en français standard, puis répondez par écrit.
checklist: Every contraction rewritten (chais pas, t'as, y'a, faut, y'aura, t'es, j'suis)
A friendly reply with a question

models.label: Model answer
models.fr:
En français standard : « Salut ! Je ne sais pas si tu as vu, mais il y a un spectacle gratuit au parc samedi. Il faut arriver tôt, il y aura beaucoup de monde. Es-tu partant ? Écris-moi, je suis au travail jusqu'à 18 h. »

Ma réponse : Salut ! Je n'avais pas vu, merci ! Oui, je suis partant. On se donne rendez-vous à l'entrée du parc vers 17 h ? J'apporterai une couverture et quelque chose à boire. Bonne fin de journée au travail !
models.en:
In standard French: “Hi! I don't know if you saw, but there's a free show in the park on Saturday. We have to get there early, there will be lots of people. Are you in? Write to me, I'm at work until 6 p.m.”

My reply: Hi! I hadn't seen it, thanks! Yes, I'm in. Shall we meet at the park entrance around 5 p.m.? I'll bring a blanket and something to drink. Have a good rest of the day at work!

blocks.prompt: Listen again to Sofia's voice message in the Discover step. Then retell it in your own words in clear, standard French, as if you were explaining to a colleague what Sofia said.
checklist: Report speech: Sofia dit que… / Elle explique que…
Full forms only (il y a, il faut que, je ne sais pas)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Sofia dit qu'elle est épuisée. Il y a eu un problème sur le serveur à trois heures, et elle doit tout recommencer demain matin. Elle explique donc qu'elle ne sait pas si elle peut aller au cinéma avec Mei. Elle propose plutôt samedi, et elle demande à Mei de lui envoyer un texto.
models.en: Sofia says she's exhausted. There was a problem on the server at three o'clock, and she has to start everything over tomorrow morning. So she explains that she doesn't know if she can go to the movies with Mei. She suggests Saturday instead, and asks Mei to send her a text.

summary:
- Recognize the four processes of fast speech: dropped [[ne]], dropped [[e]], merged sounds ([[chais pas]]), shrunken pronouns ([[y'a]], [[t'es]], [[faut]])
- Decode common forms: [[chais pas]], [[j'suis]], [[y'a]], [[t'sais]], [[t'as]], [[qu'est-ce tu fais ?]]
- Grab stressed content words and rebuild the full sentence
- Recognize these forms, but always write the full standard form
